title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a short transitional page in a 1986 formal project whose vocabulary is 'ateliers' (workshops), 'magasins' (stores), 'figures', 'supports' and 'opérations matérielles' (consumption and production). The setting appears to be a lattice Σ with ∧ and ∨. It specializes to a Boolean algebra when ∧ distributes over ∨, as the previous page notes. 'Figures' (the R and G figures of p.117) carry underlying 'supports', apparently subsets or strata of some space. A 'fonction-support' assigns a support to each item.

The page does three things.

(1) It poses an open question. Does the existence of a 'faithful external support function' (defined in an earlier chapter, CF VIII p.62) imply all the 'validity' properties of workshops? It should be compared with a corollary proved earlier (CF VIII p.78, cor.1). The special case of 'faithful stores' should be examined. In modern terms: does a faithful representation of the abstract structure by supports, a kind of concrete semantics, imply soundness of all the axioms (validity conditions) of the formal system?

(2) Grothendieck postpones this. First he must push ahead, to see how the notion of support actually enters the consequences and whether it proves as crucial as he expects.

(3) He begins a 'critique philosophique' of approaching supports through 'operations'. Defining the material operations (consumption, production) forces one to combine sets or strata that need not be constructible, nor even 'commensurable', nor describable discretely or combinatorially. The next page draws the conclusion explicitly. So far supports were only treated as constructible sets, yet even the presentation X|Y involves non-constructible strata, an 'internal contradiction'. He also wants an intrinsic description of the supports underlying a figure, independent of that figure.

The page is thus an assessment of an obstacle. A combinatorial or constructible-set semantics for an axiomatic theory of production processes is not closed under the operations it needs. The setting resembles abstract resource or process theories, or a Boolean or constructible-set semantics for a lattice-valued logic. No theorem is stated or proved.
errors: No mathematical claim is asserted, so there is nothing to refute. The page itself records a conceptual gap: support operations leave the class of constructible sets. Together with the failure of transitivity of ≲ noted on p.117, this suggests the framework as set up was not yet consistent.

ideas.what: Question whether a faithful external support function (a concrete faithful representation) entails all validity axioms of 'ateliers'
ideas.modern_name: Soundness/representation question for an axiomatic structure (cf. representation theorems for lattices/Boolean algebras, concrete semantics of process/resource theories)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Representation theory of lattices: Stone, Birkhoff; resource theories: Coecke–Fritz–Spekkens (2016)

ideas.what: Observation that operations on supports (consumption/production) force use of non-constructible, non-'commensurable' strata, contradicting a purely constructible/combinatorial treatment
ideas.modern_name: Non-closure of constructible (or definable) sets under required operations; need for a larger o-minimal/definable or measurable class of supports
ideas.usually_credited_to: General (Chevalley constructibility; o-minimality: van den Dries et al.)

ideas.what: Desire for an intrinsic description of the supports underlying a figure, independent of the figure
ideas.modern_name: Intrinsic support / support of an object in a lattice-valued or sheaf-like semantics

missed.claim: Open problem: does a faithful external support function force all validity properties of workshops/stores? This is left explicitly unresolved, part of a little-known 1986 axiomatic theory of 'ateliers/magasins' with material operations of production and consumption.
missed.quote: Il faudrait voir si l'existence d'une "fonction-support externe fidèle" (CF VIII p. 62) implique toutes les validités des Ateliers
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It may be of interest to historians, and possibly to researchers on resource theories or Petri-net semantics, if the 'ateliers' project formalizes production processes. The page alone is too fragmentary to establish any mathematical content beyond the question.

deep.surprise_reason: The page belongs to an obscure, little-documented 1986 formal project on 'ateliers' and 'magasins' with production and consumption operations. That project is itself somewhat unexpected. But this page contains only a deferred question and a self-critique about constructibility of supports, with no result.

'(CF VIIII p. 62)' is most likely 'CF VIII p. 62' (an extra stroke); consistent with 'CF VIII p. 78' below
'pour me rendre compte comment[?] certaines[?] conséquences[?]' – the first word may be 'combien'; reading uncertain
'des ... qui ne sont pas nécessairement[?] compatibles[?]' – the last word is plausibly 'constructibles', given the next page's discussion of 'supports constructibles'
'les raisons[?] des supports' – plausibly 'les notions de supports'
